name: Hedgehog pathway agonist
lead: Hedgehog pathway agonists are small molecules that switch on Hedgehog signaling, the pathway that guides embryonic development and regulates adult stem cells. They were explored as topical hair-growth compounds because activation of the pathway is reported to be required for hair follicles to move from the resting phase into the growth phase, the step that would lead to thicker, fuller hair [1].

A 2005 paper titled 'Modulation of hair growth with small molecule agonists of the hedgehog signaling pathway' is cited in connection with this approach [1]. In community discussion the program is associated with Curis and Procter & Gamble. Wikipedia states that the hair-growth effort ended because of toxicities found in animal models, without naming the compound or the sponsor [1].
No hedgehog agonist hair product has reached the market, and no human efficacy results have been published.
infobox: Development reported as ended on animal toxicity [1]

paras: In the Hedgehog pathway, the receptor Patched-1 suppresses Smoothened; when Sonic hedgehog binds Patched-1, Smoothened is released and activates GLI transcription factors. Small-molecule agonists and antagonists acting on Smoothened are used to study this regulation [1]. Approved drugs vismodegib (January 2012) and sonidegib (July 2015) inhibit Smoothened for basal cell carcinoma, and Wikipedia describes the class as having harmful and potentially toxic side effects [1].

Agonists work in the opposite direction to these inhibitors. Wikipedia reports that pathway activation is required for the follicle's transition from resting to growth phase [1]. Sonic hedgehog is also described as regulating dermal fat formation by hair follicle transit-amplifying cells [2].

Wikipedia states that exploiting the pathway for hair growth failed due to toxicities seen in animal models; the sentence cites a corporate investor-relations page [1]. The association with Curis and Procter & Gamble comes from how the program is labelled in community discussion, and no published source located names the compound.
No studies found. The only related work is the 2005 preclinical paper on hair growth modulation with small-molecule agonists [1].

timeline.event: Paper on small-molecule Hedgehog agonists modulating hair growth published. [1]

card.summary: A discontinued class of topical hair-growth compounds that activated Hedgehog signaling; development reportedly ended over animal toxicity.
card.note: Not available as a product; no human efficacy data found.

quick.overview:
Hedgehog pathway agonists were explored as hair-growth agents because the pathway helps follicles enter the growth phase.

Wikipedia says the effort failed on animal toxicity. No human results were found.
quick.mechanism: They activate Smoothened/GLI signaling, the opposite of anticancer Smoothened inhibitors such as vismodegib.
quick.risks: The reported reason for stopping was toxicity in animal models. Pathway activation in general is a concern in tissue-growth contexts, and no product is available.

chain: A small molecule activates Smoothened / Hedgehog signaling in the follicle
Follicles are pushed from the resting phase into the growth phase
More growing follicles, aiming at thicker hair
angle.text: The goal of the approach was a topical treatment that wakes resting follicles to grow hair. It remains a research concept; no product is available to use.
